source.title: Good Classifiers are Abundant in the Interpolating Regime
source.authors: Ryan Theisen; J. Klusowski; Michael W. Mahoney

record.tranche_reason: The paper mentions double descent as background and cites prior work, but its own results characterize test-error distributions among interpolating classifiers; they do not test any of the stated double-descent versions.
record.gate_note: The paper varies training-sample counts and random-feature counts, but reports test-error distributions conditional on interpolation, not a fall-rise-fall risk curve over size, epochs, or sample size. Its double-descent examples are citations to other work. The retained rows are the paper's own test-error findings that do not establish any listed version.
record.test_reason: The paper cites double-descent work (including BHMM19) only as background. Its own results are distributions of test errors among interpolating classifiers sampled uniformly from the version space, always with n < d or n/N = α < 1. It never plots risk against model size, epochs or sample size across the interpolation threshold, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors also conclude that worst-case/uniform-convergence analysis does not reflect typical generalization, and that statistical-mechanics approaches are a promising alternative. They conjecture that a critical value ε*(α) exists in general.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes distributions of test errors among interpolating classifiers; it does not apply the original double-descent measurement as a test of the stated curves.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported critical value depends on task difficulty and aspect ratio α; in the Gaussian model it depends on the data correlation and sample count.

fits_no_version.finding: Among interpolating linear and random-ReLU-feature classifiers, test errors concentrate around a critical value ε*(α) as dimension or feature count grows. Worst-case interpolators with near-total error exist but are rare.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Typical interpolating classifiers generalize well, and their test-error distribution concentrates at a critical value depending on the aspect ratio n/N.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
record.problems: The empirical test-error distributions are largely presented in figures, with no reported uncertainty estimates for the reported results. The paper does not evaluate the double-descent curves in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: Other test-error distribution plots and additional dataset/task examples in Figures 2, 4–9 are not separately extracted because the text does not state their numeric values or distinguish individual plotted conditions sufficiently for reliable row-level assignment.
record.verdict_notes: ε* depends on α = n/N, which could in principle relate to sample-wise or capacity curves. However, the paper does not report ε* as a function of α across the threshold, and all settings stay at n < d.

versions.untested_parts: Model-wise fall-rise-fall test-error curve and peak near the interpolation threshold.
Whether adding training samples near an interpolation threshold raises test error.
Risk curves across model classes as capacity crosses the interpolation point.
Whether a single effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations.
Noise and regularization effects on peaks, multiple descent, or removal of peaks.
Whether effective parameter counting turns second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

relation.reason: The introduction cites double-descent findings as background; the study neither tests their curves nor uses them as a tool.

tranche.reason: The results characterize typical and worst-case errors among interpolating classifiers, without testing any listed double-descent version.
